chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus, from Is'haq ibn Ammar, from Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him), he said:
I said to him: One hundred and ninety Dirhams, and nineteen Dinars — is there any zakat upon it?

So he said: When gold and silver combine and that reaches two hundred Dirhams, then zakat is due on it, because the essence of wealth is the Dirhams, and everything apart from the Dirhams — whether gold or chattels — is a commodity referred back to the Dirhams in matters of zakat and blood money (diyat).

key_terms.الدَّرَاهِمُ: Dirhams — silver coins serving as the standard monetary unit in classical Islamic law
key_terms.الدِّيَاتِ: Diyat (blood money) — compensatory payments in Islamic law for loss of life or bodily harm
key_terms.عَرْضٌ: Commodity/trade goods — non-monetary assets converted to their dirham equivalent
key_terms.عَيْنَ الْمَالِ: The essence/actual form of wealth — the primary currency of valuation
key_terms.مَرْدُودٌ: Referred back/converted — the legal technique of reducing non-monetary wealth to its dirham value
key_terms.نِصَاب: Nisab — the minimum threshold of wealth at which zakat becomes obligatory

ai.seo_question: What is the zakat ruling when gold and silver are combined in Shia Islamic law?
ai.summary: Imam al-Kazim (peace be upon him) establishes the ruling that when gold and silver are combined, they are assessed together against the nisab (minimum threshold) of two hundred Dirhams for zakat purposes. The Imam's principle that the Dirham is the 'essence of wealth' reflects the classical Shia jurisprudential position that silver currency serves as the universal standard for calculating both zakat thresholds and blood money (diyat) compensation. This combines two distinct but related domains of Islamic financial law under one unifying principle.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail Bin marrar, from Yunus, from Is’haq Bin Ammar, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ibrahim<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘
I said to himasws, ‘One hundred and ninety Dirhams, and nineteen Dinars, is there any Zakāt on it?’

So heasws said: ‘When there gathers the gold and the silver, and that reaches to two hundred Dirhams, so regarding these is the Zakāt, because the essence of the wealth is the Dirhams, and everything apart from the Dirhams, from gold or chattels, so it is dealt with by referring that to the Dirhams with regards to the Zakāt and the compensations’.
en.sarwar: 8. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ’Isma‘il ibn Marrar from Yunus from Ishaq ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following: “I once said to abu Ibrahim, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, ‘There is one hundred ninety dirham and nineteen dinar.

He (the Imam) said, ‘If gold and silver together amount to two hundred dirham, then there is Zakat payable, because dirham represents the value of wealth and items other than dirham like gold and goods are evaluated on the basis of dirham in matters of Zakat and compensations.’”
